question: On what exact historical date did the word of the LORD come by Haggai the prophet, and to which two civil and religious leaders of Judah was it addressed?
opt1: In the second year of Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day; unto Zerubbabel governor of Judah, and Joshua the high priest
opt2: In the first year of Cyrus, in the seventh month, on the tenth day; unto Ezra the priest, and Nehemiah the cupbearer
opt3: In the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, in the third month, on the fifth day; unto Sanballat the governor, and Eliashib the high priest
opt4: In the fourth year of Darius, in the ninth month, on the fourth day; unto Zechariah the prophet, and Hananiah the ruler of the palace
correct: In the second year of Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day; unto Zerubbabel governor of Judah, and Joshua the high priest
explanation: Haggai's prophecy began on the New Moon of the sixth month in Darius II's second year (520 BC), addressed to Zerubbabel and Joshua. Haggai 1:1 (KJV) - "In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the LORD by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, saying,"

question: What common, procrastinating excuse among the returned exiles did the LORD of hosts quote and confront in Haggai 1:2?
opt1: "This people say, The Persian king hath forbidden our work until the walls of Jerusalem be finished"
opt2: "This people say, The time is not come, the time that the LORD's house should be built"
opt3: "This people say, We have no silver nor gold to purchase cedar beams from the merchants of Tyre"
opt4: "This people say, The seventy years of Jeremiah are not yet fulfilled, therefore let us abide in peace"
correct: "This people say, The time is not come, the time that the LORD's house should be built"
explanation: The people rationalized their spiritual apathy by claiming the timing was not right to rebuild God's temple. Haggai 1:2 (KJV) - "Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, This people say, The time is not come, the time that the LORD's house should be built."

question: With what piercing rhetorical question did the prophet expose the selfish disparity in their building priorities in Haggai 1:4?
opt1: "Why build ye ivory palaces in the mountains of Judah, while the altar of the Holy One is covered with dust?"
opt2: "Shall mortal man feast in chambers of cedar, while the Ark of the Covenant remaineth under curtains?"
opt3: "Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?"
opt4: "Have ye forgotten the ruins of Zion, that ye adorn your own dwellings with the carved wood of Lebanon?"
correct: "Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?"
explanation: God rebuked them for living in luxurious paneled (cieled) houses while His temple remained a desolate ruin. Haggai 1:4 (KJV) - "Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?"

question: In the famous charge "Consider your ways", what tragic economic paradoxes did Haggai identify in verse 6?
opt1: Gathering harvests devoured by locusts, digging wells that yield salt water, and weaving fine linen ruined by moth and rust
opt2: Planting vineyards trampled by wild boars, buying silver that turns to dross, and building cisterns that can hold no water
opt3: Trading with foreign merchants for counterfeit gold, baking bread with blighted wheat, and herding flocks consumed by wolves
opt4: Sowing much but bringing in little, eating without being filled, drinking without satisfaction, clothing without warmth, and earning wages put into a bag with holes
correct: Sowing much but bringing in little, eating without being filled, drinking without satisfaction, clothing without warmth, and earning wages put into a bag with holes
explanation: God highlighted how neglect of His house caused continuous economic frustration, like putting wages into a purse full of holes. Haggai 1:5-6 (KJV) - "Now therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways. Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes."

question: What practical instructions did the LORD give to remedy their neglect, and what divine outcome did He promise in Haggai 1:8?
opt1: "Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the LORD"
opt2: "Send messengers to Hiram of Tyre for cedar trees, and lay foundations of polished stone; and I will bless your harvest"
opt3: "Collect a half-shekel from every man of Judah, and cast bronze vessels for the altar; and I will dwell in your midst"
opt4: "Fast forty days in the valley of Kidron, and offer burnt bullocks upon the pavement; and I will turn away your reproach"
correct: "Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the LORD"
explanation: The people were commanded to fetch mountain timber and rebuild the house so God would take pleasure and be glorified. Haggai 1:8 (KJV) - "Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the LORD."

question: Why did their harvest expectations fail, and what did God personally do to their brought-in produce according to Haggai 1:9?
opt1: They trusted in Egyptian grain and God sent mildew, because they offered lame animals upon the bronze altar
opt2: They looked for much and it came to little, and God blew upon it, because His house was waste while each ran to his own house
opt3: They withheld the holy tithe and God sent caterpillars, because the priests had corrupted the covenant of Levi
opt4: They traded with Samaritan merchants and God cursed their barns, because they allowed foreigners into the inner court
correct: They looked for much and it came to little, and God blew upon it, because His house was waste while each ran to his own house
explanation: Because God's house was neglected while individuals scrambled for their own homes, God actively blew away their meager produce. Haggai 1:9 (KJV) - "Ye looked for much, and lo, it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the LORD of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house."

question: What natural and agricultural judgments did the LORD summon against the land and people in Haggai 1:10-11?
opt1: Torrential floods that washed away terrace walls, pestilence among sheep, and severe hail that shattered olive orchards
opt2: East winds that withered fig trees, blight upon barley, and swarms of locusts devouring all spring pastures
opt3: Heaven stayed from dew, earth from fruit, and a drought upon land, mountains, corn, new wine, oil, men, cattle, and all hand labor
opt4: Fiery sirocco winds that dried mountain springs, murrain among oxen, and unseasonable snow upon the vineyards
correct: Heaven stayed from dew, earth from fruit, and a drought upon land, mountains, corn, new wine, oil, men, cattle, and all hand labor
explanation: God called for a comprehensive drought upon crops, livestock, and all human labor because of their spiritual neglect. Haggai 1:10-11 (KJV) - "Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit. And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn, and upon the new wine, and upon the oil, and upon that which the ground bringeth forth, and upon men, and upon cattle, and upon all the labour of the hands."

question: How did Zerubbabel, Joshua the high priest, and the remnant of the people respond to Haggai's message in Haggai 1:12?
opt1: They questioned the prophet's authority, demanding a sign from heaven before laying aside their private building projects
opt2: They held a council of elders in Jerusalem, deciding to petition King Darius for official permits and Persian timber subsidies
opt3: They offered fifty rams upon the altar of burnt offering, but postponed construction work until the coming spring rains
opt4: They obeyed the voice of the LORD their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet as sent by God, and the people did fear before the LORD
correct: They obeyed the voice of the LORD their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet as sent by God, and the people did fear before the LORD
explanation: In rare biblical obedience, the leadership and people promptly heeded God's voice and reverently feared the LORD. Haggai 1:12 (KJV) - "Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the LORD their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the LORD their God had sent him, and the people did fear before the LORD."

question: What brief yet supremely empowering message did Haggai, the LORD's messenger, deliver unto the obedient people in Haggai 1:13?
opt1: "I am with you, saith the LORD"
opt2: "Fear not, for the kingdom is yours, saith the LORD"
opt3: "Behold, my glory shall fill this valley, saith the LORD"
opt4: "The days of your affliction are ended, saith the LORD"
correct: "I am with you, saith the LORD"
explanation: God answered their obedience with the ultimate covenant promise of His presence: 'I am with you'. Haggai 1:13 (KJV) - "Then spake Haggai the LORD's messenger in the LORD's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the LORD."

question: What spiritual catalyst enabled the community to begin rebuilding the temple, and on what exact date did construction commence?
opt1: A decree of financial grant arrived from Susa; commencing work on the first day of the seventh month, second year of Darius
opt2: The LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the remnant; commencing work on the 24th day of the sixth month, second year of Darius
opt3: A miraculous spring of water burst forth beneath the altar; commencing work on the tenth day of the seventh month, second year of Darius
opt4: The prophets Zechariah and Malachi blew silver trumpets; commencing work on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, second year of Darius
correct: The LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the remnant; commencing work on the 24th day of the sixth month, second year of Darius
explanation: Just twenty-three days after Haggai's first sermon, God stirred their spirits and work began on the 24th day of the sixth month. Haggai 1:14-15 (KJV) - "And the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the LORD of hosts, their God, In the four and twentieth day of the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king."

question: What discouraging historical comparison did the LORD address on the final day of the Feast of Tabernacles in Haggai 2:1-3?
opt1: "Why weep ye for the cedar palaces of Solomon, when the Lord of hosts hath prepared a tabernacle of light in the heavens?"
opt2: "Is not this stone altar more precious than the gold of Ophir which Nebuchadnezzar carried away into the house of his gods?"
opt3: "Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?"
opt4: "Doth any man among you remember the singing of the Levites, and think that God hath forgotten the covenant of David?"
correct: "Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?"
explanation: Elderly Jews who remembered Solomon's magnificent temple were prone to weep seeing the modest new structure as 'nothing'. Haggai 2:1-3 (KJV) - "In the seventh month, in the one and twentieth day of the month, came the word of the LORD by the prophet Haggai, saying, Speak now to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and to the residue of the people, saying, Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?"

question: With what triple command to be strong did God encourage the builders, and what ancient covenant reality remained among them?
opt1: Be strong and courageous, turn not to right or left, for "my angels encompass your walls as a shield of brass: fear ye not"
opt2: Be strong in faith, build with gladness, for "the glory of the cherubim hath returned unto the mercy seat: fear ye not"
opt3: Be strong, gird your swords, for "the chariot of God is twenty thousand, even thousands of angels: fear ye not"
opt4: Be strong Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all people of the land, and work, for "I am with you ... so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not"
correct: Be strong Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all people of the land, and work, for "I am with you ... so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not"
explanation: God anchored their strength in the Exodus covenant, reassuring them that His Holy Spirit remained actively present among them. Haggai 2:4-5 (KJV) - "Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the LORD; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the LORD, and work: for I am with you, saith the LORD of hosts: According to the word that I covenanted with you when ye came out of Egypt, so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not."

question: What cosmic shaking and glorious arrival did the LORD of hosts prophesy would fill this modest house with glory in Haggai 2:6-7?
opt1: "Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory"
opt2: "In the fullness of time I will open the windows of heaven, and pour out the treasures of the Gentiles to adorn my sanctuary with jasper"
opt3: "Behold, I will shake the mountains of Lebanon and the islands of the sea, and twelve kings of the east shall bring their tribute to Zion"
opt4: "I will send forth the Branch of righteousness with fire, and the kings of the earth shall prostrate before the threshold of my house"
correct: "Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory"
explanation: God promised a cosmic shaking of nations leading to the coming of 'the desire of all nations' (the Messiah) to fill the house with glory. Haggai 2:6-7 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD of hosts; Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: What divine claim of sovereignty over wealth is proclaimed, and what superior glory and blessing is promised for the latter house in Haggai 2:8-9?
opt1: "All the cattle upon a thousand hills are mine ... This house shall endure longer than the pillars of heaven ... and here will I forgive iniquity"
opt2: "The silver is mine, and the gold is mine ... The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former ... and in this place will I give peace"
opt3: "The cedars of Lebanon and stones of Ophir are mine ... The beauty of this house shall surpass all kingdoms ... and here will I judge the heathen"
opt4: "The wealth of the nations is my footstool ... This temple shall never be destroyed by fire ... and here will I establish David's throne"
correct: "The silver is mine, and the gold is mine ... The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former ... and in this place will I give peace"
explanation: Because silver and gold belong to God, the latter house would surpass Solomon's in spiritual glory through the Prince of Peace. Haggai 2:8-9 (KJV) - "The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts. The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: In the priestly Torah inquiry, what was the ruling when asked if holy meat carried in a garment skirt transmits holiness to common food it touches?
opt1: The priests answered and said, "Yea, it shall be sanctified unto the LORD"
opt2: The priests answered and said, "Only if it touch bread or wine during a feast day"
opt3: The priests answered and said, "No" (holiness is not transmitted by secondary contact)
opt4: The priests answered and said, "It shall be holy if washed with pure running water"
correct: The priests answered and said, "No" (holiness is not transmitted by secondary contact)
explanation: According to the Levitical law, ceremonial holiness cannot be transmitted through secondary contact. Haggai 2:11-12 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Ask now the priests concerning the law, saying, If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt do touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat, shall it be holy? And the priests answered and said, No."

question: What was the priestly ruling regarding ritual defilement from a corpse, and how did Haggai apply this principle to the nation's offerings?
opt1: The priests answered, "It remaineth clean until evening"; and Haggai declared that their sins would be cleansed at sunset
opt2: The priests answered, "Only if touched with unwashed hands"; and Haggai declared their ceremonies void without water cleansing
opt3: The priests answered, "It is pardoned by a sin offering"; and Haggai declared that two turtle doves would cleanse the altar
opt4: The priests answered, "It shall be unclean"; and Haggai declared that so was this nation and every work of their hands and offerings unclean before God
correct: The priests answered, "It shall be unclean"; and Haggai declared that so was this nation and every work of their hands and offerings unclean before God
explanation: While holiness is not contagious, ritual uncleanness is easily transmitted; hence, the people's neglect defiled all their labors and sacrifices. Haggai 2:13-14 (KJV) - "Then said Haggai, If one that is unclean by a dead body touch any of these, shall it be unclean? And the priests answered and said, It shall be unclean. Then answered Haggai, and said, So is this people, and so is this nation before me, saith the LORD; and so is every work of their hands; and that which they offer there is unclean."

question: What agricultural shortfalls and divine afflictions had plagued them prior to laying a stone upon a stone in the temple in Haggai 2:16-17?
opt1: Expectations of 20 measures yielded but 10, winepresses of 50 vessels yielded but 20; and God smote them with blasting, mildew, and hail
opt2: Expectations of 100 bushels yielded but 30, olive presses of 40 flagons yielded but 10; and God smote them with locusts and drought
opt3: Expectations of 50 measures yielded but 25, granaries of 100 bags yielded but 40; and God smote them with cankerworms and blight
opt4: Expectations of 10 measures yielded nothing, vats of 20 flagons yielded 5; and God smote them with burning winds and sulfur
correct: Expectations of 20 measures yielded but 10, winepresses of 50 vessels yielded but 20; and God smote them with blasting, mildew, and hail
explanation: Before resuming temple construction, their grain and wine yields suffered 50% to 60% deficits due to blasting, mildew, and hail. Haggai 2:15-17 (KJV) - "And now, I pray you, consider from this day and upward, from before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the LORD: Since those days were, when one came to an heap of twenty measures, there were but ten: when one came to the pressfat for to draw out fifty vessels out of the press, there were but twenty. I smote you with blasting and with mildew and with hail in all the labours of your hands; yet ye turned not to me, saith the LORD."

question: From what exact milestone date does God promise an immediate reversal of agricultural barrenness into divine blessing in Haggai 2:18-19?
opt1: From the first day of the seventh month, the Feast of Trumpets: "from this day will I multiply your seed"
opt2: From the 24th day of the ninth month, the day the temple foundation was laid: "from this day will I bless you"
opt3: From the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement: "from this day will I pour out rain in due season"
opt4: From the fourteenth day of the first month, the Feast of the Passover: "from this day will your barns overflow"
correct: From the 24th day of the ninth month, the day the temple foundation was laid: "from this day will I bless you"
explanation: Even though crops and trees had not yet produced, God declared: 'from this day will I bless you' from the foundation-laying date. Haggai 2:18-19 (KJV) - "Consider now from this day and upward, from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, even from the day that the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid, consider it. Is the seed yet in the barn? yea, as yet the vine, and the fig tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree, hath not brought forth: from this day will I bless you."

question: In Haggai's final message delivered specifically to Zerubbabel, what geopolitical upheaval and military collapse does the LORD predict?
opt1: Sending a fiery tempest upon the capitals of Media and Persia, with legions of archers blinded and cast into the sea
opt2: Drying up the Euphrates and Tigris, turning the empires of the east into desolate marshes trampled by wild beasts
opt3: Shaking heavens and earth, overthrowing thrones and strength of heathen kingdoms, with chariots, horses, and riders falling by the sword of his brother
opt4: Dividing the Greek and Egyptian coalitions with pestilence, while angelic hosts defend the mountain of Jerusalem
correct: Shaking heavens and earth, overthrowing thrones and strength of heathen kingdoms, with chariots, horses, and riders falling by the sword of his brother
explanation: God promises to shake global empires, causing opposing armies to self-destruct through civil strife ('by the sword of his brother'). Haggai 2:21-22 (KJV) - "Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, I will shake the heavens and the earth; And I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, and I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the heathen; and I will overthrow the chariots, and those that ride in them; and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother."

question: With what exalted Messianic investiture and royal token does the Book of Haggai conclude in verse 23?
opt1: "In that day will I crown thee with the golden crown of David, O Zerubbabel my prince, and establish thy kingdom from sea to sea, saith the LORD of hosts"
opt2: "Behold, I will give thee the keys of the house of David, and thou shalt open and none shall shut, O Zerubbabel my shepherd, saith the LORD of hosts"
opt3: "And thou shalt sit upon the throne of judgment in Mount Zion, and all the kings of the earth shall bow down before thee, saith the LORD of hosts"
opt4: "In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the LORD of hosts"
correct: "In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the LORD of hosts"
explanation: Reversing the curse on Jehoiachin (Coniah) in Jeremiah 22:24, God restores the Davidic lineage by making Zerubbabel His chosen signet ring. Haggai 2:23 (KJV) - "In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the LORD of hosts."
